raw_response.printed_headline_estimate: Univariate one-sample goodness-of-fit chi-square tests within individual villages only (total N = 336 households: Enqabeni n = 205, Madiba n = 131; PDF Page 5): Madiba water source (70% open water bodies vs 30% community borehole), X2 = 21, df = 1, p < 0.0001; daily water use >45 L in Madiba (78%), X2 = 122, df = 2, p < 0.0001, and Enqabeni (90%), X2 = 300, df = 2, p < 0.0001; water transport method in Enqabeni, X2 = 125, df = 2, p < 0.0001, and Madiba, X2 = 61, df = 2, p < 0.0001. No exposure-outcome inferential contrast is reported.
raw_response.publication_year_note: Published 21 February 2024 in Frontiers in Water, Vol. 6, Article 1354477 (received 12 December 2023; accepted 05 February 2024; copyright 2024).
raw_response.rationale: Although the study reports SPSS chi-square (X2) statistics and p-values on PDF Page 5 (N = 336 households across Enqabeni, n = 205, and Madiba, n = 131), every inferential test is a univariate one-sample goodness-of-fit test comparing observed category proportions against equal expected frequencies within a single village (respondent age, employment, income source, water source type in Madiba, daily water volume category, and water transport mode). No bivariate or multivariable statistical test links any legal, constitutional, municipal-governance, assistance, or corruption exposure (Criterion 2) to household or community water access (Criterion 4); institutional, infrastructural, and corruption barriers (PDF Pages 6-10) are reported exclusively via descriptive frequencies (e.g., 100% uniform agreement) and qualitative thematic content analysis. Thus there is no SWiM-eligible exposure-outcome contrast.
